T.lead: Big changes often start with small signs.
T.story: The Miller family wants to sell their old farm by the creek. A company wants to build a data center there.
T.todayMore: Some are signs of the project. Some are just everyday changes.
T.about: Notice the Signs is stop 1 of Community Builders of Pecan Grove, a free bilingual game for ages 8-14. Players compare a road last month and today and find small signs that a big project may be coming. They learn that not every change is about the project.
T.pastLine: This is the road last month. Now tap Today.
T.todayLine: Tap only the new things that could be about the farm project.
T.askLine: Ask a grown-up: what could this mean?
T.everyRest: Good eyes, but it isn't about the farm. Not every change is about the project.
T.review: Here are the signs you didn't find. Tap one to read it.
T.can: I can notice when something in my town is changing.
T.tipEvery: Next time, ask yourself: is this new thing about the farm's land?
T.tip100: Sharp eyes! Try a new round.
T.real: With a grown-up, look for one sign of change on your street or in the local news this week. Talk about what it might mean.
T.guText: Kids practice noticing change without jumping to conclusions. In Georgia, a rezoning usually comes with a public notice in the newspaper, and often a sign on the land, before the public hearing. Ask together: what is changing, and where can we read more?
